title: The indwelling presence
hookLine: the presence of God in the world, often pictured as feminine

lines: GOD IN THE MIDDLE OF THE CAMP.
cards: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them." That's God speaking to Moses in the book of Exodus, in the desert, before a single tent pole has gone up. Some readers have stopped on the last words.

Not in it, in the building. Among them, in the people. A tent of cloth and wood, carried from camp to camp, and the promise is that God will live in the middle of all that walking and arguing and cooking.
The rabbis gave that nearness a name that echoes the verse's own word for dwell.

teach.b: Shechinah. The indwelling presence of God. First, the rabbis' word for God close at hand.
Pirkei Avot teaches that when people sit together and their talk is words of Torah, the Shechinah rests among them. Not in a temple. At a table.
Second, it goes where the people go.
The Talmud says that wherever Israel was exiled, the Shechinah went into exile with them. The presence doesn't stay behind in a ruined building. It packs its bags.
The last of the ten lights is Malchut, kingship, the one that touches the world, and kabbalists identify it with the Shechinah. Every light above flows down into her. And notice the her.
Kabbalists picture the Shechinah as feminine: a queen, a bride, sometimes a mother.
Some Jews welcome the Sabbath on Friday night with songs that greet a bride and a queen, and kabbalists heard the Shechinah in those images. Fourth, the longing.
In kabbalistic teaching, the Shechinah is in some sense separated, in exile, and human deeds of Torah, prayer and kindness help reunite her with the Holy One above.
A reader might hear it this way: every good act, a little homecoming.
In this teaching, the God without end, from a few days ago, is also the presence at the table.

how: Jews speak of the Shechinah in prayer and study, and some families, following a custom of the kabbalists, sing to welcome the Sabbath as a bride and queen on Friday evening.

games.q: God tells Moses: make Me a sanctuary. where does the verse say God will dwell?
o: in the building, and nowhere else.
games.why: "that I may dwell among them." some readers stop on those words: in the people, not only in the tent.

practice: Let your eyes move slowly around the space you're in, the light on the wall, the chair, the sounds from outside, and any people near, without looking at them too hard.
Then rest your attention on the whole room, the space everything is sitting in. If you pray, you can hold the words from Exodus, that I may dwell among them; if you don't, just notice being here.
